description: Superman exercise guide for men: lift arms, chest and legs a little to train back muscles and glutes. Covers mistakes plus easier and harder versions.
intro: The superman is done lying face down: you lift your arms, chest and legs a little, hold briefly and lower. It strengthens the back muscles and glutes that hold your trunk and pelvis upright. It does not train the pelvic floor directly, but it balances the front-focused core work in a routine.
feel: You should feel the muscles along your spine and your glutes working evenly. You should not feel a sharp pinch in your lower back, your neck crank upward or your breath stop. Keep your eyes on the floor just ahead of you. If your lower back feels compressed, lift less.

mistakes.right: A few centimeters is enough. Let the glutes and back do the work instead of cranking the lower spine.
Keep your neck long and gaze down so your head moves with your chest.

mistakes.wrong: Holding your breath at the top
mistakes.right: Breathe out as you lift, breathe normally through the hold, and lower slowly.

easier: Lift only the arms and chest, or only the legs, or one arm and the opposite leg at a time.
harder: Hold the top for three to five seconds, lower over three seconds, or add a gentle Kegel during the hold and fully relax as you come down.
who: Useful for men who sit a lot or lift weights, men over 40 who want a stronger back, and anyone whose routine is mostly front core work.
skip: Skip it or use the easier version if arching hurts your lower back, after recent back, abdominal or pelvic surgery, or with a hernia. See a doctor or physiotherapist if back pain lingers after exercise. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: What does the superman exercise work?
faq.a: The muscles along your spine, your glutes and the backs of your shoulders. It is a back-strength move, not a pelvic floor one.

faq.q: Is the superman bad for your lower back?
faq.a: Not when the lift is small and controlled. Big, fast arches can irritate the lower back, so keep it low and slow.
